title: A practical workflow for coordinating fleets of coding agents
friendlyTitle: How one developer keeps many coding agents organised
summary: Fatih Arslan describes a Git-based planning system that moves work through drafts, ready plans, active execution, completion and discard states. Long-running coordinator agents dispatch isolated workers, while human-readable Markdown files preserve decisions, dependencies, handoffs and verification steps.
friendlySummary: The workflow stores plans as simple files in Git. Coordinator agents send clear tasks to other agents and record what happened.
whyItMatters: Running more agents does not remove coordination work; it makes explicit state and ownership more important. A small, reviewable plan repository can keep humans in control while allowing replaceable agents to pick up bounded work without relying on one conversation’s memory.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A shared list of plans, decisions and results helps people understand what every agent is doing. It also makes unfinished work easier to continue.
